conclusion.justification: The report concludes that arthroscopy does not provide significant clinical benefit for knee osteoarthritis and is no more effective than placebo or conservative treatments, clearly rejecting the claim.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
**Conclusion:**

Based on current evidence, arthroscopy (joint endoscopy) does not provide significant clinical benefit for patients with osteoarthritis of the knee and is generally not recommended as a standard treatment. 

Multiple randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and systematic reviews have demonstrated that arthroscopic procedures (such as lavage or debridement) are no more effective than placebo or conservative treatments in relieving pain or improving joint function. A landmark placebo-controlled trial published in the New England Journal of Medicine found no difference in outcomes between patients who underwent actual arthroscopic surgery and those who underwent sham surgery. 

Consequently, major medical guidelines advise against the routine use of arthroscopy for knee osteoarthritis. For example, the UK's National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) recommends against the procedure for the vast majority of osteoarthritis patients, a position supported by a Cochrane review. While some surgeons suggest it may benefit a select group with mild osteoarthritis and specific meniscal injuries, the overarching consensus from high-quality evidence is that arthroscopic surgery is not superior to non-surgical management for this condition.

**Sources:**

*   Moseley JB, et al. A Controlled Trial of Arthroscopic Surgery for Osteoarthritis of the Knee. New England Journal of Medicine. https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa013259
*   Cochrane. Arthroscopic surgery for degenerative knee disease. https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD014328_arthroscopic-surgery-degenerative-knee-disease
*   Barlow T, et al. Why we still perform arthroscopy in knee osteoarthritis: a systematic review. PMC. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4435528/
*   Arthroscopic surgery is not superior to conservative treatment in knee osteoarthritis: a meta-analysis. BMC Musculoskeletal Disorders. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12891-024-07813-3
